Series::igamma¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::igamma(const Series& other) const
Series Series::igamma(double other) const
Series& Series::igamma_(const Series& other)
Series& Series::igamma_(double other)
Series& Series::igamma_(const Series& other) const

What It Does¶

Computes the regularized lower incomplete gamma function P(a, x) elementwise. self supplies the shape parameter a; the argument supplies the upper limit x:

P(a, x) = ( 1 / Gamma(a) ) * integral_0^x t^(a-1) e^(-t) dt

The regularization by Gamma(a) puts the value on [0, 1], and P(a, .) is exactly the cumulative distribution function of a Gamma(a, rate 1) random variable. So igamma is how you get Gamma, chi-square, and Erlang tail probabilities: the chi-square CDF with k degrees of freedom is P(k/2, x/2).

Behaviour:

  • P(a, 0) = 0 and P(a, x) -> 1 as x -> inf; the function is monotone increasing in x.

  • P(a, x) + Q(a, x) = 1, where Q is igammac, the upper tail.

  • Defined for a > 0 and x >= 0. Outside that the result is NaN.

The double overload treats x as a constant broadcast against every element of a.

The Series overload follows ordinary broadcasting. This matters when a column of shape parameters is evaluated at a row of integration limits: the result is a table whose rows are distributions and whose columns are evaluation points.

Parameters¶

other (const Series& or double): the upper limit x, broadcast against self.

Returns¶

Series or Series& A Series broadcast over a and x, each element P(a, x) in [0, 1]. The in-place forms write the broadcast result into self and therefore require the broadcast shape to equal self.shape().

Integral inputs are promoted for out-of-place evaluation. In-place evaluation requires floating storage.

Gradient¶

igamma is differentiable with respect to x (the other argument, when it is a Series). Differentiating the integral by its upper limit:

d/dx P(a, x) = x^(a-1) e^(-x) / Gamma(a)

which is the Gamma(a, 1) density at x.

There is no gradient with respect to a (the shape parameter): that derivative has no elementary closed form and is not wired. If self tracks slope and x does not, an objective built only from igamma is disconnected from its input, and calling reverse() on it raises. The igamma(double) overload holds x constant, so it is non-differentiable in the same way.

In-Place Form¶

igamma_() is the in-place sibling of igamma(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — igamma_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
auto y = pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0});

x.igamma_(y);
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0.63212056, 0.26424112]

Examples¶

Example 1. With a = 2 fixed, P climbs from 0 toward 1 as x grows.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0})
        .igamma(pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0, 3.0, 20.0}))
) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.2642, 0.8009, 1.0000]

Example 2. The lower and upper tails sum to 1.

auto a = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.5});
auto x = pluss::make_series({0.3, 1.0, 4.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.igamma(x).add(a.igammac(x)));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000]

Example 3. At a = 1 the incomplete gamma collapses to the exponential CDF, P(1, x) = 1 - e^(-x).

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0, 1.0}).igamma(x));
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.neg().exp().neg().add(1.0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.3935, 0.6321, 0.8647]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.3935, 0.6321, 0.8647]

Example 4. The backward pass with respect to x is the Gamma density x^(a-1) e^(-x) / Gamma(a).

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
pluss::make_series({2.0, 2.0}).igamma(x).sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0.3679, 0.1494]

With a = 2, the density is x e^(-x): 1 * e^(-1) = 0.3679 and 3 * e^(-3) = 0.1494.

Example 5. Broadcasting a [2,1] column of shapes against three limits builds a [2,3] CDF table. The first row has a = 1; the second has a = 2.

auto shapes = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0}).reshape({2, 1});
auto limits = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, shapes.igamma(limits)) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 0.3935 0.6321 0.8647 ⎤
⎣ 0.0902 0.2642 0.5940 ⎦

Example 6. Exact endpoints pair naturally with the complementary function. At x = 0, all mass is in the upper tail; at x = +inf, all mass is in the lower tail.

auto a = pluss::make_series({2.0, 2.0, 2.0});
auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 3.0,
                             std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.igamma(x)) << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.igammac(x)) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.8009, 1.0000]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 0.1991, 0.0000]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Argument order is a.igamma(x): self is the shape parameter, the argument is the integration limit. Swapping them silently computes a different value.

  • Gradient flows only through x, and only when x is a Series. There is no gradient with respect to a; an objective that depends on a alone through igamma is disconnected and reverse() raises.

  • a <= 0 or x < 0 gives NaN.

  • For the upper tail (survival function) use igammac rather than 1 - igamma, which loses precision when P is close to 1.

  • In-place broadcasting cannot enlarge the receiver. If broadcasting a and x would create a larger shape, use igamma() and keep the returned series.

Summary¶

igamma(x) is the regularized lower incomplete gamma P(a, x), with a from self:

  • the CDF of a Gamma(a, 1); chi-square CDF is P(k/2, x/2)

  • rises from 0 to 1 in x; P + Q = 1 with igammac

  • NaN for a <= 0 or x < 0

  • differentiable in x with backward x^(a-1) e^(-x) / Gamma(a); not differentiable in a

  • the double overload holds x constant and is non-differentiable

See Also¶

  • Series::igammac: the complementary upper tail Q(a, x).

  • Series::lgamma: the Gamma(a) normalizer, in log space.

  • Series::erf: P(1/2, x^2) is erf(x), a special case.
